path_analysis: The physical IN list contains a column and CASE expression. try_evaluate_constant_list receives array-valued expressions on the empty batch, so it returns None. InListExpr evaluates this list using the dynamic Arrow-comparison path.

CaseExpr selects ExpressionOrExpression for a single WHEN whose THEN is a column and ELSE is a non-null literal. ScalarOrScalar requires two literals, and InfallibleExprOrNull requires the ELSE branch to be absent.

The selected CASE path filters THEN and ELSE batches and calls arrow_select::merge. merge rebuilds alternating results through MutableArrayData::extend. extend dispatches both validity and value callbacks even when the chosen validity callback is a one-instruction return.

The fifteen compared hot functions have identical normalized instructions and named relocation targets across the two binaries. Their locations differ. This comparison covers roughly 88%-89% of sampled cycles, not every instruction, data address or processor state.
Profile proportions locate work; they do not establish which function causes a roughly one-percent end-to-end difference.

import hashlib
import json
import mmap
import re
import struct
import subprocess
from pathlib import Path

p = Path(__file__).parent
q = p.parent / 'float-in-hash-884522f'
profiles = json.loads((p / 'profiles.json').read_text())
top = re.search(r'^\s+[\d.]+%\s+\[.\]\s+(.+?)\s+-\s+-\s*$', profiles[0]['report'], re.M).group(1)
selected = json.loads((p/'selected-functions.json').read_text())
records = [{'name': name} for name in selected]
sha = lambda data: hashlib.sha256(data).hexdigest()
for variant in ['before', 'after']:
    binary = q / f'{variant}-bench'
    symbols = subprocess.check_output(['nm', '-SC', '--defined-only', str(binary)], text=True)
    (p / f'{variant}-symbols.txt').write_text(symbols)
    rows = [row for line in symbols.splitlines() if len(row := line.split(maxsplit=3)) == 4]
    names = {int(row[0], 16): row[3] for row in rows if int(row[0], 16) != 0}
    with binary.open('rb') as file, mmap.mmap(file.fileno(), 0, access=mmap.ACCESS_READ) as elf:
        assert elf[:6] == b'\x7fELF\x02\x01'
        section_offset = struct.unpack_from('<Q', elf, 0x28)[0]
        section_size, section_count = struct.unpack_from('<HH', elf, 0x3a)
        relocations = {}
        for i in range(section_count):
            section = struct.unpack_from('<IIQQQQIIQQ', elf, section_offset + i * section_size)
            if section[1] != 4:  # SHT_RELA
                continue
            for at in range(section[4], section[4] + section[5], section[9]):
                address, info, addend = struct.unpack_from('<QQq', elf, at)
                if info & 0xffffffff == 8:  # R_X86_64_RELATIVE
                    relocations[address] = addend
        for n, record in enumerate(records):
            found = [row for row in rows if row[3] == record['name']]
            assert len(found) == 1
            start, size = [int(x, 16) for x in found[0][:2]]
            assembly = subprocess.check_output(['objdump', '-d', '-C', '--no-show-raw-insn', '-Mintel',
                                               f'--start-address={start}', f'--stop-address={start + size}', str(binary)], text=True)
            normalized, resolved = [], {}
            for line in assembly.splitlines():
                instruction = re.match(r'^\s*([0-9a-f]+):\s+(.*)$', line)
                if not instruction:
                    continue
                op = instruction[2]
                slot = re.search(r'#\s+([0-9a-f]+) <_DYNAMIC[^>]*>', op)
                if slot:
                    target = relocations[int(slot[1], 16)]
                    name = names[target]
                    resolved[slot[1]] = {'target': hex(target), 'name': name}
                    op = op[:slot.start()] + '# <' + name + '>'
                op = re.sub(r'\[rip[+-]0x[0-9a-f]+\]', '[rip+relocation]', op)
                op = re.sub(r'\b[0-9a-f]+ <', '<', op)
                normalized.append(f'{int(instruction[1], 16) - start:04x} {op}')
            normalized = '\n'.join(normalized) + '\n'
            record[variant] = {'start': hex(start), 'size': size, 'alignment_mod64': start % 64,
                               'normalized_sha256': sha(normalized.encode()),
                               'instruction_count': len(normalized.splitlines()), 'resolved_slots': resolved,
                               'normalized': normalized, 'assembly': assembly}
            (p / f'code-{n}-{variant}.txt').write_text(assembly)
            (p / f'normalized-{n}-{variant}.txt').write_text(normalized)
for record in records:
    record['normalized_equal'] = record['before']['normalized'] == record['after']['normalized']
(p / 'code-comparison.json').write_text(json.dumps({
    'method': 'Compare instruction offsets and operations, remove link addresses from named calls and RIP references, and resolve anonymous GOT slots using ELF R_X86_64_RELATIVE relocations and symbol names. This checks selected function bodies, not the entire executable or runtime data placement.',
    'functions': records,
}, indent=2) + '\n')
for record in records:
    print(record['before']['instruction_count'], 'instructions; equal:', record['normalized_equal'], record['name'][:140])
